rationale:
The test adequately checks `requirements.test-coverage.index.guidance`.

**Obligation.** The generated coverage subchapter must make coverage-collection and post-suite-checking guidance available. The guidance must follow `requirements.test-coverage.check.guidance`. It must appear without separate authored content. That cited requirement is context only. Its content defines what the guidance has to say.

**Test.** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` carries a `{test}` reference to the subject. It starts from a book with only a bare parent chapter and a stub source file. The fixture has no authored coverage page or coverage content. It calls `populate_in` and then reads the generated `coverage` chapter's `content`.

**Assertions.** The test asserts that the generated content contains each of these guidance fragments:
- `habeas test`, `habeas coverage -- --workspace` and `habeas coverage-check`.
- The sequencing text: "after it succeeds,\nrun `habeas coverage-check` as a separate step". This matches the "recommend running coverage-check after a successful workspace run as a separate step" clause.
- The text "`habeas test` collects coverage for the whole workspace,\nthen checks it". This matches the clause documenting `habeas test` as collection followed by checking.
- "static validation test needs no prior coverage". This matches the clause that the static validation test does not depend on collected coverage or on running last.

It also asserts that no unexpanded `:::{coverage-index}` directive remains in the generated content. That shows the page was generated rather than left as authored placeholder text.

**Variants.** The test runs both with and without a section number, so it covers the two modes the generated subchapter can be placed in.

**Gaps.** I found none. Every distinguishable part of the obligation has a matching assertion. The "no authored content" condition is covered by the fixture itself. I did not read the `fixture()` helper source, so I am assuming it builds a book with no authored coverage content, as the test body suggests.
